diagrams.title: Lean showcase topology
diagrams.summary: A public, static learning surface is separated from authenticated, metered Azure execution.
diagrams.boundary: Original application design. The 900-second session and three daily starts are application policies, not Entra token settings.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages
nodes.detail:
Static HTML / CSS / JS
Public catalog and atlas

steps.text: GitHub Pages serves public learning content; only the backend may call paid services. GitHub hosting is a user-selected boundary, not a Microsoft-hosting claim.
Entra External ID supplies email-OTP authentication. Backend approval, token validation, a non-renewable 900-second application session and three starts per UTC day remain custom requirements.
Conditional ledger writes precede paid work. A global spending reservation and a per-identity session transaction must not be mistaken for one cross-partition transaction.
AI modules are activated only after price, quota, regional and access checks. The architecture does not promise a hard Azure billing cap.

decisions: Keep secrets and paid execution out of the public origin.
Use durable, idempotent accounting rather than browser timers or process memory.
Separate usage telemetry from admission control; delayed billing data cannot enforce a real-time allowance.
limitations: Not deployed. Authentication, quotas and live execution remain unimplemented.
This is not a complete production security or private-network design.
AI tools, retrieval, media, Fabric and Purview are not automatically included in the $100 target.

diagrams.title: Enterprise private-connectivity pattern
diagrams.summary: A simplified adaptation of Microsoft's baseline Foundry chat architecture, not a replacement for its full network design.
diagrams.boundary: Service icons on the right represent managed PaaS resources. They are not depicted as compute deployed inside the workload VNet.

steps.text: The baseline routes inbound traffic through Application Gateway/WAF to an App Service chat UI. The UI authenticates to Foundry using managed identity and private reachability.
Standard agent setup uses workload-owned network and dedicated agent-managed resources. Application session/quota tables must be separate from agent-managed stores.
The agent can query AI Search, invoke its model, and persist conversation items. Public tool egress requires the baseline's outbound controls; private tool paths remain private.
This enterprise pattern has a separate cost and reliability profile. It is not silently included in a consumption demo budget.

decisions: Use the complete Microsoft baseline for subnet sizing, DNS, egress, access, availability and deployment details.
Keep agent-managed state exclusive to Agent Service.
Treat private networking as connectivity control, not a substitute for authorization.
limitations: Adapted excerpt, not Microsoft's unmodified official diagram or a deployable network specification.
DNS, individual private endpoints, availability zones, build infrastructure and detailed routes are intentionally not expanded.
No enterprise resources or private endpoints have been provisioned.

diagrams.title: Visitor admission and session sequence
diagrams.summary: Authentication, application session admission, and paid-action authorization are three distinct decisions.
diagrams.boundary: The short application session is independent of identity-token lifetime. Unknown accounting, expired sessions and exhausted allowances must deny paid work.

steps.text: External ID manages email OTP. Successful authentication does not imply that this application's visitor allowlist or spending policies have approved access.
A successful, idempotent start reserves one of three sessions for the approved identity in a UTC calendar day. The API sets an absolute expiry 900 seconds after creation.

Each paid action checks expiry and reserves bounded usage before provider execution. Use ETags and partition-aware transactions; compensate or safely retain failed reservations rather than permit overspend.
Streams, voice and tool loops must stop at the application deadline. Refreshing an identity token must not extend that deadline.

decisions: Treat 900 seconds and three daily starts as repository policy, not Microsoft service defaults.
Never claim cross-partition atomicity in Azure Tables.
Use explicit rejection paths for approval, capacity, quota, price or ledger failures.
limitations: Sequence specification only; no OTP, session or payment enforcement is implemented.
OIDC/MSAL protocol exchanges are intentionally abstracted; a real implementation must validate access tokens for its configured issuer/audience/scopes.
Three identities do not prove three distinct humans; approval and abuse controls remain necessary.

diagrams.title: Grounded agent request sequence
diagrams.summary: Trace the path from an authenticated UI through retrieval, model execution, conversation state and a grounded response.
diagrams.boundary: This adapts the baseline's agent workflow. Source references must be validated; a model answer alone is not evidence that a source supports it.

steps.text: The App Service caller uses managed identity and the baseline's private path to invoke the agent with the user query and conversation context.
Agent Service orchestrates the configured search tool, then its configured language model with relevant grounding context. The diagram does not assume public search or anonymous data access.
Under standard agent setup, Agent Service manages the dedicated Cosmos DB conversation store. It is not a general application session database.
The UI receives the result and any available source references. Application acceptance should check relevant evidence, citations, policy failures, empty retrieval and timeouts.

decisions: Treat retrieved text as untrusted input, not authorization or executable instructions.
Keep conversation retention separate from the short visitor-session contract.
Include negative cases and evidence checks in the eventual evaluation harness.
limitations: Conceptual ordering; internal model/tool iterations can vary by agent configuration.
No claim is made that references guarantee truth or that this repository has passed live grounding evaluations.
Agent Service standard setup is distinct from a minimal basic demo setup.

diagrams.title: Business ontology and source bindings
diagrams.summary: A fictional commerce vocabulary makes entity types, properties, relationships and their source bindings explicit.
diagrams.boundary: Ontology supplies business context, not a new general-purpose query engine. Graph materialization is optional, not automatic.

nodes.detail:
Agents / dashboards

steps.text: Define reusable entity types and typed properties in the synthetic demo.commerce namespace. An entity type is a definition; an entity instance is a data-backed occurrence.

Declare Customer places Order, Order contains OrderLine, and OrderLine refers to Product. The illustrated one-to-many business intent is a demo contract, not an asserted automatic Fabric cardinality constraint.
Bind identifiers and relationship properties to governed source tables. Direct-column or mapping-table bindings depend on the relationship and supported source shape.
Supported consumers use the ontology's context and authorized bound sources. A graph schema does not automatically load instance data; opt-in graph execution needs separate decisions.

decisions: Do not confuse an ontology, a relational schema, a Purview glossary, a vector index or an LLM prompt.
Natural-language ontology rules convey context; enforceable quality/security constraints still need explicit implementation.
Keep source-owned calculations and access controls at their authoritative sources.
limitations: Fabric IQ ontology is preview, not a Foundry-native capability or deployed component of this repo.
Requires appropriate Fabric capacity, item permissions, tenant settings and supported bindings.
The downloadable synthetic model is explanatory JSON, not a supported Fabric import or deployment format.

diagrams.title: Quality-gated knowledge publication
diagrams.summary: Separate data refinement, governance assessment and an explicitly owned publication gate before AI retrieval.
diagrams.boundary: Purview assesses configured quality rules. Blocking publication and quarantining data are explicit pipeline responsibilities, not an automatic Purview side effect.

groups.label: Microsoft Fabric / OneLake - separate refinement layers
Governance, enforcement and consumption are different responsibilities

nodes.detail:
Rule evidence + explicit policy
Approve, stop or remediate

nodes.label: Azure AI Search
nodes.detail:
Approved retrieval snapshot
Version / lineage / access

edges.label: Configured scanning of supported Fabric assets

steps.text: Preserve source data in bronze; standardize and validate in silver; publish curated products in gold. Separation and ownership are deliberate parts of the medallion pattern.

Register and scan sources, assign a data product, configure a quality connection, profile, define rules and run assessments. Purview can assess supported Fabric lakehouse/Delta data subject to source, identity and regional prerequisites.

Measure the documented dimensions: completeness, consistency, conformity, accuracy, freshness and uniqueness. Use rule-specific semantics; uniqueness alone can ignore nulls without an empty/blank check.

Implement the owned gate before indexing. Fabric transformation constraints can FAIL or DROP records; explicit quarantine, thresholds, sign-off and publication orchestration remain workload decisions.
Record dataset version, rule version, scan evidence, owner and approval with the retrieval snapshot. A high quality score is not proof of factual truth, safe access or grounded model output.

decisions: Do not publish on an unknown, failed or stale quality assessment.
Distinguish source-data quality from ontology semantics and LLM answer evaluation.
Define accuracy against an authoritative oracle; use known synthetic truth only for local examples.
limitations: Reference architecture only: Fabric/Purview capacity, connectors, scans and indexing are not provisioned.
Regional co-location, managed-identity permissions, supported formats and current connector restrictions require preflight verification.
Example thresholds are demo policy, not Microsoft defaults or measured cloud scores.
